newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Jardine sells j/v stake to Australia's ColMut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Jardine sells j/v stake to Australia's ColMut.

text.p: Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd said on Friday that Australian financial services group Colonial Ltd had agreed to buy out Jardine's 50 percent joint venture stake in their Jardine CMG joint life insurance venture in Asia for US$163 million.
Jardine said it would record an exceptional profit of about US$130 million from the sale in its 1997 results.

"Colonial, through its subsidiary CMG Asia, has agreed to acquire the balance of Jardine CMG for a total consideration of US$163 million (A$215 million)," Jardine and Colonial said in a joint statement. Jardine CMG has wholly-owned operations in Hong Kong and Singapore and has further ventures with local partners in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand.

Jardine's listed Philippines' subsidiary, Jardine Davies Inc, would sell its 40 percent interest in Jardine CMG's Life Insurance Company Inc to Colonial for US$15 as part of the overall US$163 million transaction.

"Of the total consideration, 25 percent will be payable upon completion, which is set for February 28 pending regulatory approvals and Jardine Pacific has agreed to fund the balance for up to two years," Jardine said.
"Jardine Pacific will record a net exceptional profit of some US$130 million in respect of the transactions in its 1997 result.
Colonial said later in the statement the purchase would be largely financed by a capital issue when it listed in the second quarter of 1997.
Colonial and Jardine said they had both benefited from the partnership and would be pleased to work together on future projects.

"We are please to have helped build a successful business, but feel that the time is right for Jardine Pacivic to unlock the value built up in the investment so as to concentrate more fully on businesses where we can bring more added value," Jardine Pacific Chairman Anthony Nightingale said in the statement.
Colonial Managing Director Peter Smedley said the acquisition would help position Colonial in the lead-up to listing on the Australian Stock Exchange in the second quarter of 1997.
"We wanted to provide investors with a greater stake in the growth markets of Asia," Smedley said in the statement.
